operator_io_quirks: Column name with spaces and mixed case: Tasks."eg Agree Objectives" (VARCHAR(1), all NULL) — must be double-quoted in generated SQL; case-insensitive lookup must still find it.
All identifiers are backtick-quoted in DDL; generated SQL must use double quotes, so read_schema must strip backticks and keep original spelling.
Project_Staff.staff_id is declared DOUBLE but is the PRIMARY KEY and stores integral reals (0.0, 3.0, 29.0) — Number fuzzer with float perturbation will produce non-integer PKs; sqlite accepts them.
Project_Outcomes has NO primary key (pk=[]) — sample_fresh_primary_keys must be a no-op there; drop_unique_duplicates also no-op (no unique cols).

Project_Outcomes.outcome_details, Project_Staff.other_details, Tasks."eg Agree Objectives" are 100% NULL (distinct=0, storage=['null']) — original_values lists are all None; Base sampler drops None -> empty elements -> p:=1 (always fresh).
Documents.other_details has distinct=1 with sample '' (empty string) — String sampler with one element and length range [0,1].

DATETIME columns store text 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS' (with time component); ts_fuzzer dispatch is 'Date|Number(int elements)' — first element parses as int? No (has '-'), so Date fuzzer with template %Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S.
Grants.grant_amount DECIMAL(19,4) has mixed storage ['real','integer'] — Number fuzzer scale=19, precision=4, is_int=False; range [-1e19,1e19] huge.
FK Documents.grant_id -> Grants.grant_id: parent has 15 rows, child 15 rows, child distinct=8 (many-to-one) — FK fill draws with replacement from parent's final values, so duplicates expected.
FK Project_Outcomes.project_id -> Projects.project_id: parent 15 rows, child distinct=10; Project_Outcomes has no PK so no dedup.
All FK parents exist (parent_exists=true everywhere); no dangling FKs, no self-references, no composite keys in this DB.
Small DB (all tables <=15 rows, 2-row lookup tables) — choose_table_sizes will produce sizes 1..~2500, far larger than original; original_sizes tiny.
operator_ts_expectations: Date fuzzer on all DATETIME columns: template '%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S' from first parsable element; range = [min,max] of parsed elements (e.g. 1970..2016) — fresh dates stay in that narrow window, so queries filtering outside it (e.g. year>2020) get 0 rows -> FN.

String fuzzer on VARCHAR(10) code columns (document_type_code, organisation_type, role_code, outcome_code): fresh random strings over a-zA-Z0-9() of length 0..10, plus contaminate — values like 'APP','REG','RES','SPON','Paper','Patent','leader','researcher' will be diluted; equality joins on these codes still work via FK fill but WHERE code='APP' may miss.
String fuzzer on VARCHAR(255) description/details columns: random strings, not the original English words — queries matching text patterns (LIKE '%research%') get FN.

Number fuzzer on INTEGER PKs: fresh uniform in [-1e4,1e4] (scale=4) with +-1/+-2 perturbation — PKs become large/negative, so queries with id<10 or BETWEEN small ranges get FN; joins still consistent via FK fill.
Number fuzzer on grant_amount DECIMAL(19,4): range [-1e19,1e19] — SUM/AVG/MAX comparisons against plausible amounts (e.g. >1000) become trivially true or false -> FP/FN.
Number fuzzer on Project_Staff.staff_id DOUBLE PK: float perturbation +-0.01/+-0.02 — non-integer PKs; queries staff_id=3 (int) may miss due to 3.0 vs 3.01.

FK fill draws with replacement from parent's FINAL filtered values — Documents.grant_id gets duplicates (many-to-one), matching original distinct=8<15; but if parent PK dedup drops rows, child may get NULLs (empty parent) -> NOT NULL insert failures skipped -> fewer rows.

NOT NULL not enforced in Python: rows violating NOT NULL (e.g. Documents.sent_date NULL from empty Date elements) fail at insert and are silently skipped — table sizes shrink, causing FN on COUNT(*) queries.
Empty-string element in Documents.other_details (distinct=1, '') — String sampler returns '' often; queries other_details='' match, others miss.
All-NULL columns (Project_Outcomes.outcome_details etc.): Base drops None -> p=1 -> always fresh random strings, never NULL — queries IS NULL get FN, IS NOT NULL get FP.
Small lookup tables (2 rows) with FK children: FK fill from 2 parent values gives only 2 distinct child codes — good for join coverage, but WHERE code IN (list) may miss if list has other values.

No composite PKs, no self-FK, no dangling FK — process_order is a simple 4-level DAG (Organisation_Types/Staff_Roles/Research_Outcomes/Document_Types -> Organisations -> Grants/Projects/Research_Staff -> Documents/Tasks/Project_Outcomes/Project_Staff).
